name: Tute arrastrado
description: Tute arrastrado is a Tute variant for three or four players (with four, the dealer sits out each hand). Thirteen cards each from a 40-card Spanish pack; last card turned for trump. Follow suit and overtake or trump; after winning a trick you may sing 20 or 40 (40 before 20); tute (four kings or four horses) wins the hand outright. Chip payments: 100 or 200 from each opponent, plus 40 or 20 per declaration.

history.origins: Tute originated in Italy as tutti and spread to Spain in the 19th century, becoming one of the country's most popular card games. Tute arrastrado is an individual-play variant for three or four players (with four, the dealer sits out each hand), using the same 40-card Spanish pack and marriage-type scoring; it appears alongside other Tute variants such as corriente, habanero, and subastado in Spanish card-game literature.
timeline: 19th century: Tute spread to Spain from Italy; individual variant (arrastrado) for 3-4 players documented.

setup.players: Three players, or four with dealer sitting out each hand.
setup.dealing: Thirteen cards each, one at a time; last card turned for trump.

rules.objective: Score the most points from card values in tricks, singing (king-horse 20/40), and last trick (10). Declaring tute (four kings or four horses) after winning a trick wins the hand outright.
rules.gameplay: Player to dealer's right leads. Follow suit and overtake or trump as in partnership Tute. After winning a trick, a player may sing one 20 or 40 (king-horse of same suit); 40 in trumps before any 20. Trump 7 or 2 may be exchanged for the turned card before first trick. Winner is the player with most points; chip payments: 100 from each opponent if winner has 100 or fewer, 200 if 101 or more; 40 or 20 chips per declaration.
keyRules: Tute (4 kings or 4 horses) wins hand
